Pedagogical manuscript · Completed in 2024 · 241 pages

Pedagogical guide to social sciences

The Pedagogical guide to social sciences: social understanding and critical reflection It brings together materials developed during my teaching between 2020 and 2023 in the Sociology and Differential Education majors.

The project began as a series of notes that allowed me to connect the mandatory bibliography with the structure of each subject. Over time, these texts incorporated examples, activities, evaluations, and in-depth resources. In 2024 I finished reorganizing them as a unitary manuscript intended primarily for teachers.

Process

From notes to a guide

When I started teaching classes, I needed to build routes that articulated texts from different traditions. The notes emerged as a tool to organize this bibliography and offer a common sequence from which to develop the classes.

By sharing them with students and using them in new subjects, the materials began to transform. I added examples close to their experiences and activities that allowed them to observe, discuss and apply the concepts.

Writing the manuscript was not simply a matter of gathering those documents. It was necessary to review repetitions, complete content, establish a progression and convert materials designed for specific situations into resources that could be reused by other people.

Organization

A progressive structure

The guide is organized into four parts and eight chapters:

  1. Foundations of social sciences, with an introduction to scientific knowledge and its production.
  2. Social psychology, with content on interaction, influence and contemporary perspectives.
  3. Intersections between social sciences, focused on its relationships with education and the economy.
  4. Contemporary debates in sociology, dedicated to theoretical problems of greater complexity.

Each chapter includes learning objectives, an introduction, conceptual development, in-depth resources, activities, notes and references. The manuscript also includes a glossary that can be used to review content or prepare new pedagogical materials.

Reformulation

Recognize a change in audience

The project was initially conceived as an introductory book for students. During writing I noticed that the extension and density achieved did not always correspond to the simple reading I had imagined.

Instead of hiding that difficulty, I reformulated the manuscript as a guide for teachers. The activities, questions and resources could function as a repertoire from which to select and adapt materials for different courses.

This displacement modified the meaning of the project. The guide no longer seeks to offer a single self-sufficient introduction to the social sciences, but rather to make available an architecture of content and activities arising from a specific teaching practice.

Authorship

My contribution

I wrote and organized the entire manuscript. The work included the transformation of notes and evaluations into chapters, the selection and articulation of content, the development of examples and activities, the incorporation of in-depth resources and the construction of the glossary.

The text was developed under CIPSE-UCEN during the period in which I worked in the center. Marco Cofré wrote the prologue and Fernando Varela collaborated in the preparation of the manuscript.

Editorial status and access

Complete manuscript

The manuscript was completed in 2024 and is under contract with the Universidad Central de Chile Publishing House. The editorial process is still pending.

Scope

A selection located

The guide does not purport to represent the social sciences exhaustively. Their selection responds to the subjects I taught, the study programs I worked with and the pedagogical problems I encountered during that period.

Theoretical-practical guide · Tested with students during 2025 · 95 pages

Basic guidelines for the formulation of research projects

This text was written to accompany social science students who begin to formulate a research project. Its purpose is to make visible the logic that connects the choice of a topic, the initial exploration, the construction of a problem, the methodological decisions and the ethical safeguard.

The guide is based on a simple conviction: you learn to investigate by investigating, but the experience needs mediation, opportunities for review and spaces to talk about the decisions made.

Sequence

Build a project chapter by chapter

The text is organized into six chapters:

  1. logic of social research;
  2. choice and delimitation of a topic;
  3. exploration phase;
  4. formulation of the problem;
  5. operationalization and planning of work;
  6. ethical aspects of research.

Each chapter combines explanations, examples and activities designed to advance the construction of your own project. The exploratory phase incorporates literature review, observation, documentary review and initial interviews, so that curiosity can gradually become a researchable question.

The text also includes an introductory annex on systematic reviews and scoping reviews.

Application

Try the guide accompanying thesis

During 2025 I used a draft with ten fourth-year Psychology students whom I accompanied in the formulation of their thesis projects.

We work class by class reading the chapters and developing the activities. During the sessions I asked them what content they had found clear or difficult, what activities had been useful to them, and what aspects needed a different explanation. At the end of the course we talked about the contribution that the text had made to their thesis processes.

A pedagogical tension

Between a linear sequence and an iterative practice

The organization by chapters offers a relatively orderly image of the research process. This linearity fulfills a pedagogical function, but it is not intended to literally describe how research is carried out.

In practice, formulating a project involves going back to previous decisions, reformulating questions, ruling out alternatives, and recognizing problems that were not visible at the beginning. The guide offers an initial route to orient yourself within that process, not a recipe that eliminates your uncertainty.

Authorship

My contribution

I wrote the entire text and designed its activities. I also used it to support the thesis, I mediated the reading of its chapters and collected feedback during its application in the classroom.

The manuscript was developed under CIPSE-UCEN and had the support of the director of the Psychology degree, David Covarrubias.

Scope and access

An entry point

The text is mainly oriented to qualitative projects of initial or intermediate complexity. It does not replace specialized methodological manuals nor does it aim to cover all possible designs.

Its function is to offer an entry point and a work structure for those who need to begin converting a general interest into a reasoned, achievable and ethically responsible project.

Training experience · Economic Sociology · 2024

Build a value chain through applied research

During 2024, in the Economic Sociology subject, I proposed to the students to develop a diagnosis and formulate recommendations for an organization using the knowledge worked on in the course.

Franco González and Matías Toledo developed the project in greater depth. His work focused on the shrimp and prawn fishing value chain of the Association of Fishing Industrialists and Shipowners of Coquimbo (AIP).

Bonding

Link the classroom with an organization

I managed the initial contact with the person in charge of the Productive Development Unit of the Municipality of Coquimbo. Through this link, students were able to access the AIP and develop work with a real organization.

I proposed using the value chain approach as a framework to delimit the problem, identify actors and observe the relationships between the different links of productive activity.

The assignment thus ceased to be only an exercise in conceptual application. Students had to interact with external interlocutors, produce information and construct a representation that could be understandable to other people.

On the ground

Learn field work

I accompanied the students during a day of field work. The instance allowed teaching in a situation how to take notes, ask questions, listen to the interviewees and record relevant information without losing sight of the project objectives.

The process combined review of literature and secondary sources, development of interview guidelines, management of informed consents, and conducting interviews.

Then we work together on data analysis. The students outlined the links in the chain, identified supporting actors and organizations, selected problems and prepared a SWOT analysis.

Representation

Build the diagram through iterations

The final visualization did not appear all at once. The students prepared a version of the diagram and we reviewed it in work meetings. I pointed out problems of organization, readability or interpretation; They incorporated the corrections and presented a new version.

These iterations were interspersed with the data analysis. Modifying the figure could make visible a relationship that needed further elaboration, and a new interpretation could require rearranging the diagram.

Public circulation

Take work outside the classroom

The person in charge of Productive Development knew the result and invited us to present it at the 2nd Interdisciplinary Meeting on Sustainability and Heritage of the Coastal Communities of Coquimbo, held on July 5, 2024.

For that instance I prepared an introduction about the new economy and solidarity production chains. Its function was to offer a conceptual framework before the presentation of the diagnosis prepared by the students.

The public exhibition allowed a work initiated as a course activity to circulate to a different audience and relate to territorial conversations about sustainability, production and coastal communities.

Authorship and credits

A accompanied job

The research, analysis and final diagram were carried out by Franco González González and Matías Toledo Torres.

My contribution consisted of designing the pedagogical assignment, managing the initial link, proposing the value chain approach, accompanying the field work, supporting the data analysis and guiding the iterations of the figure. I also prepared the conceptual introduction used during the public presentation.

Document

Public presentation

The public copy brings together the conceptual introduction and presentation of the students' work. The final slide containing email addresses was omitted.
